main_text.p: τειχεσθλιὸν γε καὶ τλκαίπωγον φύσα, [?] πολλῶν τε μισθόν ἔχει ἵλεω φρονίσθων. [?]
main_text.head: VERSVS XII.
main_text.p: III. Habacuci ἔνστασις [?], in qua ostendit, nec Iudaeos tantis calamitatibus, nec Babylonios tanta felicitate dignos esse: ac proinde utrosque alio loco habendos & aliter tractandos esse.Lectio 16. 29. Septemb.

p.i: Nonne fuisti ab initio Iehovah Deus meus, Sancte meus? non moriemur, o Iehovah: ut iudicium facias, posuisti illum: & fortem ut increpares, fundasti eum.

main_text.p: In hoc versu Enthymemata duo occurrunt: quorum alterum ducitur à sanctificatione & segregatione populi Israelitici, alterum à destinato Dei in Chaldaeis excitandis. Nos Syllogismis integris utemur, ut omnia sint planiora.
main_text.head: I. ARGUMENTUM HABACUCI, DUCTUM à segregatione Israelitarum à caeteris Gentibus idololatricis.
main_text.p: Reuocauerat Dominus Deus Seruum suum ad aliarum Gentium fata consideranda: & quidem eo consilio, ut disceret,

page.notes: The Greek epigraph at the top is set in Greek type and my reading of it is uncertain; the marked words need checking against the scan. The Greek word after "Habacuci" in the III. paragraph is also uncertain. A faint, mirrored text in the right margin near the middle of the page (around "Gregorius") looks like show-through and was left out. The paragraph continues on the next page; the word "non" at the foot is the catchword.
